tagline: The world's gaming capital already moves millions across the delta by sea — and the Hong Kong↔Macau ferry is one of the densest cross-border water routes on earth. Make it fast, flat and clean.
summary: Macau is a tiny SAR with planetary-scale visitor flow — tens of millions of arrivals a year, the world's largest gaming-revenue hub, and a wall of integrated resorts along the Cotai Strip. It sits at the western mouth of the Pearl River Delta, and for decades its lifeline to Hong Kong was the sea: the TurboJET / Cotai Water Jet corridors across to Sheung Wan, Tsim Sha Tsui and HK Airport's SkyPier were among the busiest scheduled fast-ferry routes in the world. The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge pulled some volume onto the road, but the diesel ferry network across to Hong Kong, Shenzhen (Shekou) and Zhuhai is still huge, aging and ripe for a fast, smooth, all-electric foiling upgrade — a premium cross-border tier for a market that already pays for speed.

use_cases.title: Modernise the Hong Kong↔Macau crossing
use_cases.body: Replace diesel high-speed ferries on the Macau↔Sheung Wan / Tsim Sha Tsui / SkyPier legs with fast, near-silent all-electric foiling shuttles — a premium, smooth, no-seasickness tier on one of the world's densest cross-border water routes.

use_cases.title: Cotai resort-direct VIP transfers
use_cases.body: Foiling transfers straight to the Taipa (Pac On) terminal beside the Cotai Strip give VIP and mass-premium guests a fast, branded arrival from Hong Kong, the HK airport SkyPier and Shenzhen — bypassing road and border queues.

use_cases.title: Pearl River Delta cross-border grid
use_cases.body: A foiling network linking Macau ↔ Shenzhen (Shekou) ↔ Zhuhai ↔ Hong Kong turns the protected delta into a fast, clean, multi-city commuter and business surface.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Owns the entire Macau opportunity: the Hong Kong crossing (~37 nm), the SkyPier airport transfer (~33 nm), and the Shenzhen/Zhuhai cross-border legs (~40 nm) all sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, over the protected waters of the Pearl River Delta — a dense, high-frequency, pay-for-speed cross-border network.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Provides sea-state margin and refuel-anywhere reliability for the most weather-exposed open-delta legs and any extension out along the wider Guangdong coast beyond the all-electric envelope.

competitive_landscape: Macau's cross-border water market is mature and proven — TurboJET and Cotai Water Jet ran some of the busiest fast-ferry services on earth, and the resorts have long chartered premium transfers. The fleet is diesel, the ride is rough in the open delta, and the HZMB bridge has reset the competitive map. That is precisely the opening: a fast, smooth, all-electric foiling tier upgrades an adopted, high-volume, willing-to-pay water habit rather than inventing one.
seasonality: The Pearl River Delta runs a summer typhoon season (roughly Jun-Oct) that disrupts open-water ferry legs, plus year-round delta chop. Foiling adds smoothness and the resort/cross-border demand is effectively year-round, anchored by gaming and business flows that don't follow a leisure season.
regulatory_note: Macau is a Special Administrative Region with its own maritime administration (DSAMA); cross-border services touch Hong Kong, Guangdong (Shenzhen/Zhuhai) and mainland authorities. A premium foiling tier would layer onto existing licensed cross-border ferry frameworks rather than requiring new route categories.
